{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom curve of the fish, about 36 dominoes laid in five builds from the nose. It was connected all the way from the start by about the 1:45 mark. That curve forms the lower half of the body outline, which the judge needs to read the animal as a fish. The finished picture lit up about 99 of the 101 standing dominoes from the nose.

Execution: I claimed the bottom curve early and said so out loud, so nobody duplicated the work. I laid it in steady stretches and then inspected the joins. I checked the tail join area several times, at around 1:45, 2:15, 2:45 and 4:15-4:30. I also offered to take over part of the top curve if it fell behind. Once the fish was connected I kept my hands off it. The table is expected to have about one bump in a session, so I didn't touch a working chain.

Collaboration: I kept my messages short and clear about who was on what. I told Maya I would stay out of her way while she finished the top curve. I offered to meet her from the right if she needed help, and she said she didn't. I gave Leo and Priya clear space while they worked on the tail lobes. When others asked for hands-off time at a joint, I respected it and didn't crowd them.

Leadership: I set the division of labor early by taking the bottom curve and telling the others to move to the tail. I kept the group focused on the main risk, which was whether everything connected to the start. I also kept calling for hands-off time near the end so the finished piece stayed intact. I feel my part was a central piece of the result, though the top curve and tail were equally needed. I'd put my share at roughly a third.", "my_share_percent": 30}
